artifact.title: BrainGuide Evidence Dashboard — Consolidated Semantic Data Registry
artifact.purpose: Give an LLM enough semantic context to understand what the BrainGuide analytics data measures, how it is calculated, why it exists, and which conclusions are safe.
artifact.completeness_note: This is a semantic summary, not a complete row-level export. Selected tables, monthly series, campaigns, geography rows, and graph edges are summarized; the original PDFs remain authoritative for exhaustive values.
artifact.authoritative_rule: The source PDFs and dashboard definitions remain authoritative for row-level values. This registry is a semantic consolidation and should be regenerated when the dashboard changes.

executive_context.organization_and_product: BrainGuide is a public-facing brain-health information and screening-navigation platform associated with UsAgainstAlzheimer's. It helps people assess memory concerns, receive tailored educational guidance, and navigate provider or clinical-trial resources.
executive_context.central_analytics_question: Who is BrainGuide reaching, what do they need, how do they move through the platform, whether experiences differ across populations, and whether use progresses toward appropriate care or research action.
executive_context.important_clinical_boundary: AD8, MIS, and SBC values in this dashboard are screening or routing measures. A Good/Poor/Moderate label is a product result category, not a medical diagnosis. BrainGuide results do not replace clinical evaluation.
primary_uses: Monitor reach, acquisition, content demand, language access, geography, and device access.
Understand questionnaire starts, scored completions, non-scored information completions, and result routing.
Understand performance patterns within AD8, MIS, and SBC assessment flows.
Measure engagement with result pages, PDF sharing, provider navigation, and clinical-trial links.
Identify measurement gaps and hypotheses for product, content, outreach, and instrumentation work.
not_safe_to_claim_from_this_snapshot: That any page, campaign, or interaction caused a questionnaire completion or care-seeking action.
That a product result category is a clinical diagnosis.
That aggregate GA4 users can be joined to questionnaire respondents at the individual level.
That small demographic percentages are stable or representative of the population.
That pre- and post-March-2026 figures are directly comparable without a relaunch crosswalk.

fact_vs_interpretation.observed: Directly reported by a dashboard table or definition.
fact_vs_interpretation.comparative: A difference between valid groups or periods; still descriptive unless an approved design supports stronger inference.
fact_vs_interpretation.hypothesis: A plausible explanation requiring UX review, instrumentation validation, or qualitative follow-up.
fact_vs_interpretation.not_assessable: The required grain, linkage, denominator, or data quality is unavailable.

count_semantics.users: Usually distinct GA4 user_pseudo_id values in the selected period; summing daily users can double-count returning users.
count_semantics.pageviews: GA4 page_view events or the modeled pageview equivalent.
count_semantics.questionnaire_started: A respondent record/session that loaded or began the questionnaire, depending on the report. Do not equate with a scored completion.
count_semantics.received_score: A respondent completed a scored flow (AD8, MIS, or SBC) by reaching GET_SCORE or GET_SBC.
count_semantics.got_information_without_score: A respondent completed the c / Get Information path without a calculated assessment score.
count_semantics.completion_rate: Always read the report-specific denominator. Questionnaire score completion is generally Received Score divided by Started; SBC flow completion is scored entries divided by SBC flow entries.
count_semantics.not_provided: Missing, skipped, not collected for the flow, or no result URL. It is not equivalent to a negative answer.

privacy.recommended_behavior: Suppress or roll up small demographic intersections; do not use exact sparse cells to infer people.
privacy.email_rule: The Result Sharing report intentionally excludes email addresses. Contacting a person requires an authorized query outside this dashboard.
privacy.ai_rule: Do not send confidential Evidence rows or identifiers to an LLM. Provide only approved aggregate insight objects with provenance and suppression decisions.

ad8.name: Alzheimer's Disease 8-Item Informant Interview
ad8.respondent: Caregiver or family member answering about someone else.
ad8.measure: Observed change in memory and functional abilities across eight questions.

categories.label: Good
categories.meaning: Unlikely significant cognitive impairment; follow-up context still matters.

categories.label: High Concern
categories.meaning: Elevated concern flag used by this dashboard.

ad8.direction: Lower is less concern; higher is more concern.
ad8.interpretation_warning: Demographics describe the informant/caregiver, not the person being evaluated. This is a screening/routing result, not a diagnosis.

mis.name: Memory Impairment Screen
mis.respondent: Self-administered respondent in the MIS flow.
mis.measure: Memory performance using free and category-cued recall of four words.

categories.label: Good
categories.meaning: Normal memory performance in this screen.

categories.label: Poor
categories.meaning: Possible memory impairment; follow-up context matters.

word_sets.design: Four words from different semantic categories, shown in randomized presentation order to reduce association effects.

mis.interpretation_warning: The dashboard's small Spanish word-set rows are unstable and should not be compared with the large English sets without a prespecified design.

sbc.name: Speech Based Cognition assessment
sbc.measure: Continuous speech-based score from 0 to 1; higher values indicate lower risk in this product routing.
sbc.boundary_rule: The routed result page is authoritative at exact boundaries; scores exactly 0.2 or 0.5 may route to either adjacent tier.
sbc.interpretation_warning: Most people who enter SBC do not produce a scored result; abandonment or recording failure is possible. Scored-result distributions must not be generalized to all SBC entrants.

flow_c.name: Get Information without score
flow_c.measure: Completion of an information path without a calculated assessment score.
flow_c.interpretation_warning: A c-flow result URL may still map to a persona/brain-health route, but that route does not represent a scored assessment.

persona_and_routing.routing_logic: Who, diagnosis status, concern responses, and the flow-specific score category determine the result URL. Result URLs are then mapped to descriptive personas by persona_page_map.csv.
persona_and_routing.warning: Good/Poor/Moderate is a product routing label and should not be called a diagnosis or clinical outcome.

reports.what_it_measures: A visual questionnaire journey map plus qCurrent event counts, inferred step drop-off, flow structure, and upload/configuration context.
reports.why_it_exists: Lets analysts see the branching paths through Intro, MIS, AD8, SBC, and Results/Common, locate high-volume nodes, and investigate where progression decreases.
reports.population_and_grain: Event-level questionnaire transitions and qCurrent arrivals summarized as nodes and directed edges; node volume represents events/users reaching a stage, not necessarily unique people unless the underlying query defines it.
reports.coverage: The captured view describes a selected month of 2026-07-04 through 2026-08-04 and a loaded backend dataset spanning November 2024 onward.
reports.qcurrent_definition: A qCurrent event records arrival at a questionnaire screen via a button click. When there is no explicit exit event, inferred abandonment is the gap between the volume reaching one step and the volume reaching the next step.
limitations: Inferred abandonment is not a directly observed exit.
Event counts may not equal unique users without a user-level deduplication contract.
The qCurrent explorer and the modeled questionnaire outcome reports use different grains and should not be silently combined.
The markdown is a page synthesis rather than a raw export of all nodes/edges; use the dashboard/query source for complete graph rows.

reports.what_it_measures: The top-level questionnaire funnel, scored and non-scored outcomes, persona/brain-health routing, demographics, campaign attribution, and longitudinal activity.
reports.why_it_exists: This is the primary operational view of how many people start, receive a score, or complete the information path, and who reaches each result category.
reports.population_and_grain: One respondent-level modeled record summarized by date, questionnaire, flow, language, campaign/source, result, persona, and demographics; legacy pre-2024 data is monthly aggregate only.
reports.coverage: BrainGuide Standard January 2024–present; Go365 February 2025–present; legacy monthly tracking back to March 2021.
key_definitions: Started means any DynamoDB record, with start date based on earliest updatedAt.
Received Score means AD8, MIS, or SBC scored completion.
Got Information means flow c and no score.
Demographic filters apply from Received Score downward; they are not available for all starters.
The date filter uses started_date for funnel counts and completed_date for outcome/demographic analysis, so totals may not reconcile exactly.
limitations: Pre-2024 legacy data is monthly and not individual-level.
SBC frequently has no result URL, producing Not provided.
Brain-health labels derive from result URLs, not clinical diagnoses.
Go365 is a separate questionnaire/table and should be segmented from BrainGuide Standard when appropriate.

reports.why_it_exists: Shows caregiver/family concern patterns, score distribution, respondent demographics, campaign composition, and trends.

snapshot.question_with_lowest_yes_percent: Q5 Forgets correct month or year (25.8%)

The c flow has a result route but no score.

cross_report_findings.statement: Questionnaire activity is large, but the denominators differ materially by flow.
evidence: Results Overview reports 93,203 starters and 72,419 filtered records.
SBC reports 36,803 flow entries but only 1,751 scored results (4.8%).
cross_report_findings.safe_interpretation: Use flow-specific populations and denominators. Never compare raw completion counts as if they were the same cohort.

cross_report_findings.statement: Good/Poor/Moderate values are derived from product routing and score categories.
evidence: Scoring Reference maps URLs/personas to brain-health labels.
Results Overview explicitly says brain health is derived from result URL and is not a clinical diagnosis.
cross_report_findings.safe_interpretation: Describe these as product result categories or screening routes.

cross_report_findings.statement: Spanish web traffic exists but is much smaller than English traffic.
evidence: Top Content: Spanish is 5.5% of pageviews and 5.5% of users in the captured period.
Find a Provider: 194 Spanish visits vs 15,974 English.
Clinical Trials: 5,972 Spanish visits vs 44,450 English.
cross_report_findings.safe_interpretation: This supports a language-access monitoring question, not a stable performance ranking of Spanish users.

cross_report_findings.statement: Clinical-trial and provider pages have measurable outbound handoffs.
evidence: Clinical Trials: 50,422 visits and 8,331 outbound clicks, 16.5% visit-based CTR.
Find a Provider: 16,168 visits and 1,232 outbound clicks, 7.6% visit-based CTR.
Result Sharing: 3,113 shares and 225 explicit opt-ins.
cross_report_findings.safe_interpretation: These are observable engagement or intent signals. They are not trial enrollment, appointments, or downstream care outcomes.

cross_report_findings.statement: The raw GA4 export begins 2026-05-17 for event sequences and user journeys.
evidence: User Journeys and Site Events definitions.
Top Content and Result Pages use longer historical Data API backfill with different limitations.
cross_report_findings.safe_interpretation: Do not silently combine event-level post-May-17 sequence analysis with historical API aggregates as if the measurement process were identical.

known_contradictions_or_reconciliation_r.resolution: Use PyMuPDF extraction. pypdf misread the embedded dashboard font and produced private-use glyphs in place of digits; the values in this artifact were re-extracted with PyMuPDF and spot-checked against rendered pages.

known_contradictions_or_reconciliation_r.issue: Dashboard capture date vs data date
known_contradictions_or_reconciliation_r.resolution: Capture timestamps are 2026-08-06, but source marts have different latest dates. Always use the report's source coverage and freshness metadata.

known_contradictions_or_reconciliation_r.issue: Results Overview counts do not reconcile perfectly
known_contradictions_or_reconciliation_r.resolution: Started uses started_date while outcome/demographic analysis uses completed_date; date windows and source populations differ. Follow the report's explicit sanity-check note.

known_contradictions_or_reconciliation_r.issue: AD8 outcome rows do not sum to the completion KPI
known_contradictions_or_reconciliation_r.resolution: The captured AD8 outcome table shows 10,170 Poor + 2,125 Good = 12,295 versus 12,330 completions, leaving 35 records not represented in those two outcome rows. Treat the KPI and outcome table as separate reported measures until the mart's missing/unclassified rule is confirmed.

known_contradictions_or_reconciliation_r.issue: MIS outcome rows do not sum to the completion KPI
known_contradictions_or_reconciliation_r.resolution: The captured MIS outcome table shows 21,159 Poor + 86,039 Good = 107,198 versus 107,976 completions, leaving 778 records not represented in those two outcome rows. Do not assume the remainder is Poor or Good; identify the missing/unclassified score rule in the source mart.
Use result URL/routed tier at exact 0.2/0.5 boundaries; do not recompute a category from a rounded display score.
User Journeys exit means no next page_view in the session. It is not GA4 bounce rate and may be high when event-based interactions occur without page loads.
Pre-2026-05-17 or pre-2026-05-18 reports may be Data API aggregates without session-level deduplication; post-boundary raw export is internally more consistent.

known_contradictions_or_reconciliation_r.issue: Not provided vs Prefer not to answer
known_contradictions_or_reconciliation_r.resolution: Not provided can mean skipped/not collected/no result. Prefer not to answer is an explicit questionnaire option in some dimensions; education storage can make skipped and explicit refusal indistinguishable in marts.
Demographic answers are rolled to a user and attributed to every page viewed in the export window. Treat as within-group descriptive affinity, not user-level causal linkage.

before_answering: Identify the report and its population, grain, date coverage, and source.
Use the flow-specific scoring system; never merge AD8, MIS, and SBC scores.
State the numerator, denominator, and unit for any rate.
Check whether the period is historical Data API, raw GA4 export, DynamoDB, or a mixed source.
Apply suppression and mention small samples or missingness.
Use observed/comparative/hypothesis/not-assessable language rather than causal language.

safe_answer_template.measure: Metric, numerator, denominator, unit, grain, and period.
safe_answer_template.population: Who is included and who is excluded.
safe_answer_template.why_it_matters: Operational or product relevance, without overclaiming.
safe_answer_template.caveats: Source, freshness, sample size, linkage, and clinical limitations.
safe_answer_template.next_action: A validation or product action justified by the evidence.

recommended_llm_behavior.example: Observed: SBC scored-result completion was 4.8% (1,751 / 36,803 entrants) in the captured selection. Why it matters: the largest operational issue is entry-to-recording completion, not merely the risk distribution among scored respondents. Caveat: the dashboard does not distinguish abandonment from recording failure, and scored respondents are a selected subset. Next action: validate recording errors and step-level events by device and language.
